proposal: Measure the EVALUATION PROTOCOL first (split construction in cells 35-37 plus the windowing in cell 33), not the dependency pins. It is the only candidate whose defect can be proven exactly, read-only, from literals in the notebook JSON, and it decides whether the repository's own recorded result (Test acc: 24.35%, cell 39) means anything. Inferred dataset size: cell 27 builds epochs with tmin=0/tmax=50 s; cell 32's committed output prints 48 labeled epoch sets with 12 events each; cell 39 emits 115 'preloaded ... 10000 original time points' lines, so the windows_dataset has N=576 trials, each 62 channels x 10,000 samples at 200 Hz (cell 31/35 outputs), 5 classes, 100 epochs, batch 6, learning_rate 0.01, weight_decay 0.05. Cell 37 then sets train_samples=floor(0.8*576)=460, testList=range(461,576) (115 samples), and train_test_split(range(576), test_size=0.2, shuffle=False) for validation gives val=460..575 (116 samples). Therefore val n test = 115 = 100% of the test set: every test trial is also a validation trial; index 460 is validation-only; index 0 is dropped by trainList (range starts at 1) yet re-included in train_subset because train_set is reassigned to the full windows_dataset; and the train/test index sets are disjoint (0 overlap). Because the model_option and training_percent widgets are selected against the validation accuracy shown in cell 38, hyperparameter/model selection is performed on the test samples, so no reported test accuracy can be treated as held out. Second measurement: cell 27's epoch is 50 s and cell 33's trial_window_time is 50 s, so 'windowing' produces exactly one 10,000-sample window per trial; trial_window_stride_time=0.01 s has no effect, and the network input is a full 50 s trial rather than the ~1-2 s windows these architectures are normally applied to. Third: the split is by index over os.listdir order (no sort, no stratification, no subject-grouping), and there is no RNG seeding anywhere (0 occurrences of manual_seed/np.random.seed/random.seed; skorch's training loader shuffles by default), so the split and the run are not reproducible. Fourth, the recorded run itself is untrustworthy: all 43 cells have execution_count=null, the stamped run is 1724185416 = 2024-08-20 (11 days before the 'Created using Colab' commit ddfd002 on 2024-08-31), train_accuracy and valid_accuracy are pinned at 0.25 for all 100 epochs, NLLLoss is negative and grows to about -7.5e5 (impossible for NLLLoss), and the test accuracy 24.35% is exactly 28/115, consistent with a single predicted class. So the first candidate to quantify is: 'Does this notebook define a leak-free, seeded, documented evaluation split?' Static answer: no, and the artifact cannot support the article's claims as committed. Input sizes that matter for scoping any fix: 576 trials (48 files x 12 score>=4 trials), 460/116/115 train/val/test, 62 channels x 10,000 samples (50 s at 200 Hz), 5 classes, 100 epochs, batch 6, plus 6 hardcoded /content/drive paths and 0 seed calls. The minimal, highest-value follow-up would be a one-time, explicitly seeded, subject-aware split (e.g., GroupShuffleSplit/leave-subjects-out or stratified-by-class) with train/val/test index sets derived once and reused without reassignment, plus an explicit statement of the 50 s trial input. What could go wrong: (a) N=576 is inferred from output line counts because cell 33 is %%capture, so a different file set shifts the absolute counts - but test being a subset of validation is structural for any N>=2 (testList = {floor(0.8N)+1..N-1} is contained in val = {floor(0.8N)..N-1}), so the overlap finding does not depend on N; (b) recorded outputs are stale (execution_count null, timestamp predates the commit) and must be cited as documentation of a past run, never as a reproduced measurement; (c) 24.35% = 28/115 is exact arithmetic, but 'the model predicted one class for every trial' is an inference from that accuracy, not from a stored prediction vector; (d) negative NLL losses are an inconsistency to report, not a diagnosis; (e) the positional-argument semantics of braindecode's create_from_mne_epochs in 0.8/0.8.1 are not verified here - assert only the observable outcome (10,000-sample windows, one window per trial), not argument misuse; (f) do not assert a notebook-vs-article numeric mismatch until the article's actual reported numbers are quoted; (g) do not execute the notebook, and write only research/scout-explore.json.
